_comment_file: Full annotated PSD2 AIS consent object. Replace all <PLACEHOLDER> values before use. IBANs, PSU IDs, and TPP IDs must never be real data in version control.
_comment_consentId: Server-assigned unique identifier for this consent. Immutable after creation. Used as the primary key to link access tokens, audit logs, and consent receipts.

access._comment_access: Defines the exact data scope the TPP is authorised to access. The PSU sees this scope during the authorisation flow and the consent receipt.

accounts._comment: Replace with a real IBAN in a non-production environment only. Never commit real IBANs.

balances._comment: Same account — TPP is requesting balance read access.

transactions._comment: Same account — TPP is requesting transaction history read access.

_comment_recurringIndicator: true = AIS recurring consent. Governs the 90-day re-authentication requirement under PSD2 RTS Article 10. If false, this is a one-time access; validUntil can be set to today.
_comment_validUntil: The maximum date until which this consent is valid. For AIS with recurringIndicator=true, this MUST NOT exceed today + 90 days (PSD2 RTS Article 10). Format: ISO 8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD). After this date, consentStatus becomes expired and all linked tokens return 401.
_comment_frequencyPerDay: Maximum number of API calls this consent allows per day per account. PSD2 RTS Article 36 permits up to 4 AIS API calls per day per account per TPP in the absence of a user session. Set based on the TPP's use case agreed during onboarding.
_comment_consentStatus: Current lifecycle state. Valid values: received, valid, expired, revokedByPsu, revokedByAspsp, rejected. Starts as 'received' when the TPP creates the consent object. Transitions to 'valid' after PSU authorisation.
_comment_psuId: The bank's internal identifier for the PSU (payment service user). Set after the PSU completes the authorisation flow. Empty at creation.
_comment_tppId: The OAuth2 client_id of the TPP that created this consent. Used to verify that only the creating TPP can use the resulting access token.
_comment_createdAt: When the consent object was created (POST /consents). Immutable. Used to calculate the 90-day validity window and for audit.
_comment_authorisedAt: Timestamp when the PSU completed authorisation. Null until the PSU authorises. Set by the AS when the authorisation flow completes.
_comment_revokedAt: Timestamp when the consent was revoked. Null unless consentStatus is revokedByPsu or revokedByAspsp. Required for audit — regulators need to verify immediate revocation.
_comment_revokedBy: Who triggered revocation: 'PSU' or 'ASPSP'. Null until revocation. Set at the same time as revokedAt.
_comment_revocationReason: Free-text or coded reason for revocation. Examples: 'USER_REQUEST', 'FRAUD_DETECTED', 'REGULATORY_ORDER'. Null until revocation.

accessRights._comment: Immutable copy of the access scope at the time of consent creation. Stored separately from the mutable access field to preserve audit evidence even if the access field is updated.

consentReceipt._comment: Structured JSON receipt handed to the PSU at authorisation time. Documents exactly what the PSU agreed to. The bank retains this as audit evidence.

_comment_linkedTokenJtis: Array of JWT IDs (jti claims) of all access tokens issued under this consent. Populated by the AS when a token is issued. Used during revocation: each jti in this array is added to the token revocation list, immediately invalidating all outstanding tokens.
_comment_modificationHistory: Append-only array of all status transitions with timestamps and actors. Required by regulators to reconstruct the complete consent lifecycle. Never delete entries.
